title: Test engram_enabled_settings_default_blank_home_and_reject_relative_home races a real fixture launch against the 20 s production readiness deadline
outcome: The test proves blank-home default resolution and relative-home rejection without depending on a real process finishing inside a wall-clock budget, so host load can't fail it.
acceptance: The test's Save no longer launches a real Engram readiness process against ENGRAM_READINESS_TIMEOUT: its scoped default home is registered with the existing readiness seam (stage_test_engram_readiness_without_launch, src/engram_readiness_test_seam.rs), or an equivalent deterministic seam. Any other real launch the Save makes is named, and either staged or shown to have no wall-clock dependency.
The test still asserts that the blank home resolves to the scoped USERPROFILE/HOME default and that the store lands under it, and that a relative home is rejected with 400 'non-empty absolute path'.
With the seam's expired-launch half held, a stray real launch fails the test at once (not after 20 s), shown by a focused run.
Focused credited run of the test green; ENGRAM_READINESS_TIMEOUT unchanged (load_sensitive_limits.rs still pins 20 s).
The exact final input has the required independent read-only review pair with no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding, and the full gate passes on the exact committed tree.
